title: Extreme heat
tldr: Move to air conditioning or a designated cooling space, reduce exertion and drink water regularly unless your clinician restricts fluids. Confusion, collapse or seizures in heat can mean heat stroke: call emergency services and start rapid cooling.
steps: Use air conditioning, a public cooling center or another safe indoor location.
Rest, loosen unnecessary clothing and use cool wet cloths or a cool shower.
Older adults, infants, outdoor workers and people with illness may need help. Never leave anyone or pets in a parked vehicle.
For altered mental status or collapse, call emergency services and cool the person while waiting; do not give drinks to someone unable to swallow.
next: Plan activities for cooler hours and follow heat alerts. Arrange safe transport before the home becomes dangerously hot.
watch: Heat stroke can occur with sweating. Do not wait for dry skin.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Use the coolest reachable space, wet skin or cloths, reduce activity and check vulnerable people repeatedly. A closed room can become more dangerous than outdoor shade. If indoor heat becomes intolerable, move early to a safer location rather than waiting for power to return.
household: Check infants, older adults and people taking medicines that affect heat tolerance. Share the cooling plan in a form everyone can understand and name a person responsible for check-ins. Do not treat a fan or closed-window plan as suitable at every temperature.
pack_now: Prioritize supplies named in this guide that are usable by the person who needs them. Keep the checklist and relevant contact details accessible. Check carrying capacity, storage and equipment instructions in advance; collecting equipment must not delay the immediate protective action.

When the first option is unavailable

Use the coolest reachable space, wet skin or cloths, reduce activity and check vulnerable people repeatedly. A closed room can become more dangerous than outdoor shade. If indoor heat becomes intolerable, move early to a safer location rather than waiting for power to return.
faqs: Confusion, collapse or other serious neurological changes in heat can indicate heat stroke and require urgent medical help plus immediate cooling. Do not give drinks to someone who is not fully awake or cannot swallow.
The cooling center is closed — what now?

Check another cooler location and reduce exertion while arranging access. Confirm opening and transport before relying on a listed center. Do not leave a person in a vehicle while trying to solve the next step.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
